summary.text: A 72-year-old man with chronic angle-closure glaucoma, diabetes mellitus, systemic hypertension and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease had prior bilateral laser peripheral iridotomy, cataract surgery in both eyes, and right-eye retinal vein occlusion treated with monthly intravitreal aflibercept and pars plana vitrectomy for secondary epiretinal membrane. A trabeculectomy for uncontrolled glaucoma was followed by Ahmed glaucoma valve implantation in the superotemporal quadrant.

He presented with tube exposure in the right eye 1 year after Ahmed valve implantation, approximately 2 mm posterior to the limbus, with ischemic and scarred surrounding conjunctiva. At surgery the conjunctiva was immobile and the previously placed corneal patch graft had partially melted or degraded, and adjacent conjunctiva could not be advanced because of extensive ischemia.

Revision surgery was performed 3 days after tube exposure was noted: a 4-mm trephination, preparation of a partial-thickness corneal button from a residual donor rim, and suturing of the button over the tube with interrupted 10-0 nylon sutures anchored to the residual graft margin and sclera. A 4 × 3 mm temporal bulbar conjunctival autograft was harvested and secured with fibrin glue at the border of the button, partially covering it.

The authors report graft survival and reepithelialization across the corneal button, and at follow-up the tube remained fully covered with no recurrent exposure or conjunctival breakdown, with a slit-lamp photograph showing well-integrated graft and autograft. The follow-up duration is stated as 1 year in the abstract and Fig. 2 caption but 2 years in the body text and discussion.

article_limitations: Follow-up duration is stated as 1 year (abstract, Fig. 2 caption) and as 2 years (surgical technique text, discussion); kept as review-only source_conflict items.
Laterality is stated only for the retinal vein occlusion and the tube exposure (right eye); other procedures and conditions leave laterality unknown.
Supplement SD1 (CARE checklist PDF) and SD2 (surgery video) are reviewed in the supplement manifest; no clinical facts were taken from video frames.
Dates of the prior surgeries and of the revision surgery are not stated beyond the relative times recorded.
The original corneal patch graft (f031) is not tied to the Ahmed valve implantation event because the source does not say when it was placed.
The SD2 operative video final frame carries a burned-in caption reading post op year 1, agreeing with the abstract and Fig. 2 caption; no facts were taken from the video.
